questions: If multiple positions (a,b) satisfy the condition, should any valid pair be output or is there a required tie‑breaking rule (e.g., smallest a then smallest b)?
Are the indices a and b to be printed 1‑based as described, or should they be 0‑based in the output?
Must the output be separated by a space, a newline, or any other delimiter?
Is it guaranteed that at least one occurrence of T in S exists, or should we handle the case where no match is found (and if so, what output is expected)?
Are the input lines for S and T guaranteed to contain exactly N and M characters respectively without extra whitespace, and can there be leading or trailing spaces?
Can N and M be equal to 1, and if so, does the same matching rule apply for a 1×1 grid?
Should the program treat the characters '.' and '#' case‑sensitively, and are any other characters possible in the input?
Are there any time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm for the given constraints?

inline_prompts: You are given an N \times N grid S and an M \times M grid T. The cell at the i-th row from the top and the j-th column from the left is denoted by (i,j). The colors of the cells in S and T are represented by N^2 characters S_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq N) and M^2 characters T_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq M), respectively. In grid S, cell (i,j) is white if S_{i,j} is ., and black if S_{i,j} is #. The same applies for grid T. Find T within S. More precisely, output integers a and b (1 \leq a,b \leq N-M+1) that satisfy the following condition: There is exactly one valid pair (a,b); only that pair is printed. S_{a+i-1,b+j-1} = T_{i,j} for every i,j (1\leq i,j \leq M). Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M S_{1,1}S_{1,2}\dots S_{1,N} S_{2,1}S_{2,2}\dots S_{2,N} \vdots S_{N,1}S_{N,2}\dots S_{N,N} T_{1,1}T_{1,2}\dots T_{1,M} T_{2,1}T_{2,2}\dots T_{2,M} \vdots T_{M,1}T_{M,2}\dots T_{M,M} Output Print a and b. Constraints 1 \leq M \leq N \leq 50 1 \leq M \leq N \leq 50 N and M are integers. N and M are integers. Each of S_{i,j} and T_{i,j} is . or #. Each of S_{i,j} and T_{i,j} is . or #.
